label: c/r/3/f/t/d/a/e/y input late in the original phase, after a sequence opening with 2/0/n/w/q/g/l/h/b/u
explanation: Fires almost only in the original (input) phase (99% of mass), at t>=3 and mostly t=4-7; it never fires in the copy phase and only weakly on <DEL> (1% of mass). It looks like the conjunction of two things. (1) The current input comes from a preferred set: c, r, 3, f, t, d are strongest (c and r about 5.5x lift), then a, e, y, and x and j are weak. It is mostly the first occurrence of that token (93% of mass). (2) The context is a sequence that opens with tokens from a second set (2, 0, n, w, q, g, l, h, b, u). The first token has the biggest effect (first_tok=2 gives 4.1x, 0 gives 3.6x), and the second token also matters. The more of these context tokens there are, especially early ones, the more often it fires and the stronger it gets. The top activations all come in sequences opening like 2 0 w g q or 2 n 0. The context looks graded rather than all-or-nothing, so a boolean predicate loses some: precision is about 0.6 and recall about 0.55 on dev. Inputs from the preferred set in sequences that open with other letters (e.g. i, z, m, s, e) fire weakly or not at all. Inputs outside the preferred set (e.g. b, g, h, o, k, digits 0-2) essentially never fire.
